title: Micro-CT-Based Approach to Measure Body Composition and Lung Fibrosis in Mice
author: Madeleine B. Landau
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: C57BL/6 mice, 3 months old (C57BL/6J from The Jackson Laboratory, Bar Harbor, ME) Reagents
Fluriso TM , isoflurane (VETone, catalog number: 502017), store at 20–25 °C for up to five years

Oxygen [50 pounds per square inch gauge (psig) (345 kPA) to 60 psig (414 kPA) required] (air gas) Note: Oxygen can be a fire hazard, so always turn it off when not in use. Do not expose oxygen cylinders to temperatures higher than 50 °C. The oxygen tank should be securely fastened upright to prevent falling off and kept in a well-ventilated area completely separated from flammable materials and heating sources. Always keep the oxygen tank valve protected with the cap when not in use and ensure proper labeling indicating the contents as OXYGEN and whether it is full or empty. Never attempt to handle a damaged or leaking cylinder. Be aware of your laboratory-specific safety procedures while handling the oxygen tank.

Bleomycin solution 10 mg/mL in water (Sigma, catalog number: B7216); should be protected from light and stored at -20 °C. Mice were given 60 µL of bleomycin (1.25 U·kg -1 body weight) via oropharyngeal route to induce a fibrotic response that is more pronounced at day 21 after the treatment [10]. The Institutional Animal Care Use Committee (IACUC) approved this bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis protocol (Protocol ID: 1874)

steps.title: Prepare mice and bleomycin
steps.instruction: Use 3‑month‑old C57BL/6J mice; prepare 10 mg/mL bleomycin (Sigma B7216) protected from light and stored at –20 °C; administer 60 µL (1.25 U·kg⁻¹) via oropharyngeal route to induce lung fibrosis (assessment at day 21).

steps.title: Power on and warm‑up Micro‑CT
steps.instruction: Turn on the Quantum GX2 Micro‑CT system, switch safety key to On, open the Quantum GX2 Image Analysis Software and click Warm‑Up (15 min after ≤3 months disuse, otherwise 2 h).

steps.title: Create database and sample entries
steps.instruction: In the database window click Create New Database to set a folder for imaging data, then Create New Sample and enter sample information; select the sample to be scanned and click Set Image Save Location.

steps.title: Perform gain calibration if needed
steps.instruction: If the indicator is yellow/red, select Gain Calibration from Options, choose the required Scan mode, Filter and Voltage, and click Execute; the indicator must turn green when complete.

steps.title: HU calibration with water phantom
steps.instruction: a) Fill a 50 mL conical centrifuge tube with 25 mL DI water; place tube in the scanner. b) Configure Scan mode, Filter and Voltage as required, create a new sample, enter Live Mode, adjust stage to center the tube, and click Start Scan. c) After scan, right‑click the sample, select Launch HU Calibration, open ROI window, move the green AIR square to the air region and TARGET square to water, click ROI read for both, OK, close window. d) In Options → HU Calibration Settings choose the most recent calibration file; indicator should turn green.

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia with 2.5 % isoflurane (Fluriso, VETone 502017) in the RAS‑4 induction chamber; allow ~2 min for full anesthesia.

steps.title: Position mouse for body scan
steps.instruction: Place the anesthetized mouse on the mouse bed, insert the nose fully into the nose cone, close the imaging door, and ensure only one mouse is in the bed.

steps.title: Set scan parameters and orientation
steps.instruction: a) For BMD: 90 kV, 88 µA, acquisition 36, recon 36, scan mode standard (18 s), X‑ray filter Cu 0.06 + Al 0.5. b) For body composition: 45 kV, 133 µA, acquisition 36, recon 36, scan mode standard (18 s), no filter. c) Set FOV 36 mm (requires five stitched scans). d) Choose desired filter (e.g., AI 1.0 mm for fat). e) Click Initialize, then Live Mode, center the mouse using stage and rotation controls, record the stage Z position as the starting point for stitching.

steps.title: Create five‑scan stitching job
steps.instruction: Select Options > Job Scan Settings, click New, press Add to create a 5‑Job scan, enter the recorded nose Z position as start, ensure stage range (2–206 mm) is not exceeded, set Stitching On, adjust remaining parameters, click OK.

steps.title: Acquire mouse body scan
steps.instruction: In Scan Acquisition settings select the created job, verify parameters, click CT Scan, wait for standby, then remove the animal and confirm X‑RAY ON light is off.

steps.title: Scan BMD phantom
steps.instruction: Place the hydroxyapatite phantom (densities 0, 50, 200, 800, 1200 mg HA/cc) in the scanner, use the same settings as the BMD scan (90 kV, 88 µA, etc.), and acquire a scan.

steps.title: Generate phantom standard curve
steps.instruction: a) Open Quantum GX2 Database application, connect to existing database, and transfer scan files via USB or Export File. b) In Quantum GX2 Database select the phantom image, double‑click to enlarge. c) Open Analyze 14.0, click New Workspace, select Input/Output, browse to the .VOX file, click Calculate It. d) Load Volume, Exit, Rename as desired. e) Transform → Spatial Transforms → Subregion → Extract Sub‑Volume, Save Volume. f) Process → Spatial Filter → Median, Kernel Size 3, Automatic preview, Process Volume, Save Volume. g) Segment → Manual → Fabricate Shapes → 3‑D Cylinder, check Filled, adjust radius/position for each standard, Apply, Add Object to each standard, Apply. h) Save Object, open Measure, select Sample Type 3D, Enabled Objects, Stats → Size Intensity → Mean, enable Auto Log Stats, Sample Options → Sample Enabled Objects, record mean values. i) In Excel create columns “Object Name” (standard densities) and “Mean”, plot means vs densities, fit linear trendline to obtain slope (SigmaCT) and intercept (BetaCT).

steps.title: Quantify femur BMD
steps.instruction: a) Load mouse femur scan in Quantum GX2 Database, open in Analyze 14.0 as above (steps 2‑5 of phantom analysis). b) Transform → Subregion → Extract Sub‑Volume, Save Volume. c) Process → Median filter (Kernel 3, Automatic), Process Volume, Save Volume. d) Segment → Semi‑Automatic → Threshold Volume, adjust threshold to isolate bone, click Threshold Object to create bone object. e) Manual → trace to refine bone if needed, delete extraneous objects, save Object Map. f) BMA → load phantom Excel file, input SigmaCT (slope) and BetaCT (offset) as scaling parameters. g) Initial Segmentation → select saved bone object, Segment Cortex and Segment Trabeculae, then Measure Bone with default settings. h) Export measurements (auto‑saved as .CSV).

steps.title: Quantify lean and adipose tissue
steps.instruction: a) Load whole‑body scan, Transform → Subregion → Extract Sub‑Volume, Save Volume. b) Process → Median filter (Kernel 3, Automatic), Process Volume, Save Volume. c) Segment → Semi‑Automatic → Threshold Volume, adjust upper/lower limits until hypodense adipose regions appear (verify HU range from literature). d) Enable Threshold Rendering, click Threshold Object. e) Add Object → Manual → Manual Trace to encircle noise (e.g., lung, holder); for lung: Semi‑Automatic → Object Extractor → seed in lung, adjust threshold, Extract Object, then delete this object; rename original adipose object to “Fat”. f) Add Object → adjust Threshold Volume to isolate lean tissue (exclude bone and fat), enable Threshold Rendering, click Threshold Object, manually remove noise (brain, holder) as above, rename object to “Lean”. g) File → Save Object Map, exit. h) Measure → File → Load Object Map, enable Objects, Stats → Size Intensity → Volume, enable Auto Log Stats, Sample Options → Sample Enabled Objects; record volumes for Fat and Lean. i) Copy volumes into Excel to calculate % body fat and lean tissue.

steps.title: Perform lung scan with respiratory gating
steps.instruction: a) Anesthetize mouse with 2.5 % isoflurane (≈2 min). b) Place mouse on bed, close door, set scan parameters: 90 kV, 88 µA, acquisition 36, recon 36, scan mode gating (4 min), X‑ray filter Cu 0.06 + Al 0.5, FOV 36 mm (single scan). c) Select high‑speed scan mode, enable respiratory gating icon. d) Live Mode → place green ROI rectangle over diaphragm, ensure breathing interval >1000 ms. e) Start CT scan, then click Reconstruct to obtain inspiratory and expiratory phase images.

steps.title: Quantify lung volume and fibrosis
steps.instruction: a) In Quantum GX2 Database load lung image, open in Analyze 14.0 (New Workspace, Input → .VOX, Calculate It). b) Transform → Subregion → Extract Sub‑Volume to keep only lung region, Save Volume (add “_transform”). c) Segment → Semi‑Automatic → Object Extractor → seed in lung, set threshold –1294.1 to 0 HU to select whole lung, extract object. d) Threshold Volume with –1294.1 to –435 HU to isolate normally aerated lung (blue); save as object. e) Threshold Volume with –121 to 0 HU to isolate high‑density (fibrotic) lung (red); save as object. f) File → Save Object Map, exit. g) Measure → File → Load Object Map, enable Objects, Stats → Size Intensity → select Volume (and other stats as desired), enable Auto Log Stats, Sample Options → Sample Enabled Objects. h) Record volumes for aerated, non‑aerated, and moderately aerated regions; export to Excel for analysis.

description: Validation of protocol BMD calculation validation: The BMD values obtained from the calculation of the micro-CT scan of the femur cortical bone of WT mice were between 749.4 and 828.47 HA/cc. These values align with the range previously reported by Mohan et al. (845.4 ± 60.2 HA/cc) [13]. The consistency with previously reported data supports the accuracy of our BMD measurements. Fat and lean tissue calculation validation: To validate the accuracy of fat and lean tissue quantification, we scanned a WT male mouse using micro-CT and dissected out the abdominal fat and muscle from the hind limbs. The dissected fat and lean tissue were weighed, and the measured weights (fat: 1.169 g, lean: 1.385 g) matched the values calculated from the micro-CT scan (fat: 1.349 g, lean: 1.547 g). The challenges of perfect dissection can explain the differences. This result supports the accuracy of the micro-CT quantification for fat and lean tissue. Fibrosis scan validation: To validate the accuracy of fibrosis quantification, we performed a micro-CT scan and H&E staining on the same lung tissue samples. The micro-CT results showed that mice with lower aerated lung volumes had higher levels of fibrosis, as evidenced by the increased fibrotic areas in the corresponding H&E staining. This correlation between micro-CT and histological analysis supports the accuracy of lung fibrosis measurement using micro-CT.
